items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: They had a fellow named Morris French. I don't know what would come of him. He's up in Laplace.

ctx.x: Well, is anybody alive who plays much like Jack Carey, or any recordings that are much on his style?

Well, ain't but one guy that seems like Eddie Morris, probably the only one. Cause all the rest of them, probably, they, uh, the way they play trombone now, they feel like they play trompones. Yeah, they all play in the lead. Yeah, but Eddie Morris got more, you know, that style, playing sides and stuff, you know, sides. They had a fellow named Morris French. I don't know what would come of him. He's up in Laplace.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: Trombone? Well, there was a fellow named Morris French.

ctx.x: Oh, well, so you know anybody better start with, Buck. That's Bill's favorite, you know. And who did you like trombone?
Trombone? Well, there was a fellow named Morris French.
Who were some of the good trombone players down here when you were young?

Morris French, Kid Ory, Jack Keran, and let's see who else I can... Who was with Buddy Petit? Morris French was with Rene. I'm trying to... Oh, yeah, a little boy, George Washington. He never did come back. Little bit of fella. Played nice trombone.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Morris French. Morris French played Tramon with Rene.

ctx.x: Back to those brass bands here. Well, the Silverleaf brass band, they wouldn't really be playing too much music then, huh? No. Well. They'd be faking a lot of it, huh? Yeah.

Silverleaf had some good musicians. Tuxedo had some good musicians. Now, you take, well, we'd call them the Zulu band. They had a hot brass band, see? Black Benny, myself, Lewis, and what does Tramon play our name? Eddie Morris. Not Eddie Morris. Morris. Morris. Morris French. Morris French played Tramon with Rene. Yeah.
